title: The risk register decision — question explanation
learningObjective: Evaluate likelihood, impact, existing controls and residual risk systematically
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A risk register lists a low-likelihood event that could expose a large customer database. Existing controls are documented, but their current effectiveness has not been tested.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Evaluate likelihood, impact, existing controls and residual risk systematically
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option B: Assess likelihood and impact, validate existing control effectiveness, estimate residual risk and record assumptions and uncertainty. Risk assessment should consider both likelihood and consequence, then evaluate how controls change residual exposure.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Low likelihood alone ignores potentially severe impact and uncertainty about control effectiveness. Option C: Automatic maximum ratings do not provide a consistent or useful risk prioritization method. Option D: Documented controls are not necessarily effective; the risk remains until assessed and treated appropriately.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Validate control operation, document evidence and uncertainty, calculate or qualitatively rate residual risk, then assign treatment and ownership. Risk decisions require likelihood, impact, control evidence, residual risk and explicit assumptions.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Risk decisions require likelihood, impact, control evidence, residual risk and explicit assumptions.
